reason: The sources provide well-supported claims from multiple distinct sites detailing Voyager 1's trajectory, discoveries, distance milestones, and interstellar transition.
story: In 1977, NASA launched Voyager 1 on a fast-track trajectory through the Solar System. Guided by a rare alignment of outer planets occurring only once every 175 to 176 years, the probe sprinted past Jupiter and Saturn. It revealed active volcanoes on Jupiter's moon Io and detailed Saturn's complex rings. However, taking a close look at Saturn's moon Titan redirected Voyager 1 out of the ecliptic plane, ending its planetary flybys and preventing it from visiting Uranus or Neptune. On February 17, 1998, Voyager 1 overtook Pioneer 10 to become the most distant human-made object in history. Powered by nuclear generators, it snapped the iconic Pale Blue Dot portrait of Earth before shutting down its cameras. On August 25, 2012, Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause into interstellar space, carrying a Golden Record with 55 human language greetings into the galactic void.
angle: Voyager 1 sacrificed potential flybys of Uranus and Neptune to investigate Saturn's moon Titan, which launched it out of the planetary plane and into interstellar space as Earth's most distant craft.

claims.claim: Voyager 1 was launched after Voyager 2 on a shorter, faster trajectory that allowed it to reach Jupiter and Saturn earlier than its twin.
On February 17, 1998, Voyager 1 reached a distance of roughly 69 AU from the Sun and overtook Pioneer 10 as the most distant human-made object from Earth.
Gary Flandro discovered a rare planetary alignment occurring once every 175 to 176 years that allowed a spacecraft to visit all four outer giant planets using gravitational assists.
Voyager 1's electricity is supplied by radioisotope thermoelectric generators (RTGs) powered by plutonium-238.
Voyager 1 conducted primary mission flybys of both Jupiter and Saturn.
Voyager 1 discovered active volcanoes on Jupiter's moon Io, marking the first time active volcanism was observed on another body in the Solar System.
Voyager 1 made a close flyby of Saturn's moon Titan on November 12, 1980.
The trajectory chosen for the Titan flyby redirected Voyager 1 out of the ecliptic plane, ending its planetary science mission and precluding visits to Uranus and Neptune.
On February 14, 1990, Voyager 1 took the Pale Blue Dot photograph of Earth from a distance of about 40 AU.
Voyager 1 crossed the solar wind's termination shock into the heliosheath in December 2004.
On August 25, 2012, Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause to become the first human-made object to enter interstellar space.
Voyager 1 carries a gold-plated copper phonograph disc called the Golden Record intended as a message and time capsule for potential extraterrestrial life.
The Golden Record carried by Voyager 1 includes recorded spoken greetings in 55 different human languages.
On November 18, 2026, Voyager 1 reached a distance of one light-day (about 25.9 billion kilometers) from Earth.

disputed: Pioneer 10 overtake distance: S1 lists 69 AU while S3 lists 69.4 AU (attribute or omit the exact decimal).
Planetary alignment interval: S2 states once every 175 years while S4 states once every 176 years (attribute or state over 170 years).
Exact date of crossing the termination shock: S1 lists December 15, 2004, while S3 lists December 16, 2004 (attribute or state mid-December 2004).
Launch gap between twin probes: S1 states Voyager 1 launched 16 days after Voyager 2 while S4 states within 15 days (attribute or state about two weeks).
